transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date/Time: 2026-04-01 15:30 UTC
- Duration: 48 minutes
- Attendees: Jordan Blake (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Diego Morales (Redwood CSM), Maya Chen (Orpheus Head of ML), Ravi Patel (Orpheus CTO), Lena Ortiz (Orpheus SRE)

Summary and agenda (auto-gen, may be incomplete):
1) Commitment ramp & pricing structure discussion
2) Region activation (EU + APAC) and private/VPC pilot
3) Benchmarking plan (latency & throughput)
4) Security/compliance checklist and KMS integration

Transcript:
[00:00:00] Jordan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick check, can people hear me?
[00:00:04] Maya: Yep, loud and clear. thanks.
[00:00:07] Ravi: Yes, good. we got the agenda, obv want to move quickly - tight timeline on this quarter.
[00:00:15] Jordan: Great. quick refresher — Orpheus is running with Redwood hosted today in us-west, right? We saw steady traffic but you mentioned spikes during sale windows, is that still accurate?
[00:00:26] Maya: Correct. baseline is fine, but we get 3–4x spikes during promos. the p95 latency has been creeping at peak, that's our main worry.
[00:00:34] Priya: And those spikes are short-lived, yes? are you seeing sustained for more than 10 minutes?
[00:00:39] Maya: usually 7–15 minutes per event but sometimes a cascade if multiple promos. the kv cache hit rate drops under that load.
[00:00:47] Lena: to add, some of our infra routing amplifies the effect. when the CDN bounces requests to origin, we see bursty patterns hitting the inference tier.
[00:00:55] Jordan: ok that helps. so two priorities on our side today: 1) what's needed to add EU and APAC regions with predictable latency and 2) a proposal to smooth costs via a stepped commitment rather than a single big uplift.
[00:01:08] Ravi: yep, timeline is we want EU live before summer sale starting mid June, APAC is "nice to have" by Q4. we'll probably sign a 12-month commitment if the pilot and latency numbers look good.
[00:01:20] Priya: for region activation we usually do a staged path — provision dedicated capacity in eu-west-1 with autoscaling and a small canary traffic shift. private/VPC option is possible but has more ops work. are you leaning private?
[00:01:33] Maya: We want private for EU because of data residency rules and legal prefers a customer-managed VPC. For APAC we can consider hosted.
[00:01:40] Diego: noted — so hybrid: private for EU, hosted for APAC. that's common.
[00:01:45] Lena: the kicker for us is KMS integration and audit logs for requests. SOC2 is table stakes for our compliance team.
[00:01:53] Jordan: absolutely. we support KMS/HSM integrations for Private and can surface audit logs, plus RBAC and SSO. Priya will share the runbook.
[00:01:59] Priya: i'll attach the full VPC onramp doc after this call — includes firewall/IP allowlist steps and KMS key rotation notes.
[00:02:07] Ravi: great. on pricing, we need clarity on burst pricing vs reserved capacity. your current proposal showed committed GPU-hours and a separate burst bucket?
[00:02:16] Jordan: yes — our recommended model is three tiers: steady reserved capacity for baseline, reserved-burst ladder (short bursts at slightly higher unit price), and on-demand overflow which is the highest unit cost. the idea is you commit to a baseline monthly and have defined burst credits for flash events.
[00:02:31] Maya: is there a hard cap we can set so billing surprises don't happen during a sale?
[00:02:35] Jordan: you can set an account-level cap and alerts; also we can set automatic fallback to a cheaper model variant (lower-token models or stronger quantization) to keep cost steady at expense of quality.
[00:02:45] Riley: [unintelligible]
[00:02:47] Maya: who is Riley? oh nevermind.
[00:02:50] Priya: one technical note — for EU private we recommend smaller sequence lengths for the canary to optimize kernel selection and avoid unnecessary memory pressure.
[00:02:59] Lena: makes sense, we'll try trimming the max tokens for canary runs.
[00:03:03] Ravi: what about KV cache persistence across warm instances? if you scale up during burst, cold starts will hurt latency.
[00:03:10] Priya: we use prefix and KV cache warming — for dedicated pools we can pre-warm with synthetic requests. for private we can coordinate a warm-up window. also continuous batching helps reduce per-token compute.
[00:03:22] Maya: ok, so next step is a benchmark. what are we proposing?
[00:03:26] Jordan: short plan: run a 2-hour benchmark during your normal peak hour with: 1) steady-state baseline for 30m, 2) engineered spike to simulate promos for 45m, 3) cooldown and analysis. we'll measure p50/p95, tail latencies, token cost per 1k, and cache hit rate.
[00:03:40] Maya: sounds good. can we also validate private KMS integration in the same run?
[00:03:44] Priya: we can do a staged run — first run on hosted eu replica to establish numbers, then private onramp next week with KMS. integration testing for KMS will add ~1–2 hours of setup.
[00:03:55] Ravi: timeline check — if we get benchmark week of 2026-04-12 and results by 2026-04-14, can legal sign and we turn on capacity by early May?
[00:04:03] Jordan: plausible. legal usually wants SOC2 docs and a data processing addendum. we can fast-track the DPA.
[00:04:09] Maya: about SOC2, do you have a recent report we can share with legal?
[00:04:12] Jordan: yes, we'll share the most recent SOC2 Type II and the attestation. Priya — pointer where that lives?
[00:04:18] Priya: i'll drop the link to the security pack in the shared folder, includes SOC2, ISO summary, and KMS/HSM notes.
[00:04:25] Lena: there's one more thing: routing policy — we want the ability to prefer eu endpoints for users flagged by IP geolocation, but fallback to us if eu capacity is exhausted. can you do smart routing at the edge?
[00:04:35] Priya: yes, smart routing rules can be configured by policy — prefer region, and fallback chain to other regions or model variants. we can also add latency thresholds for automated failover.
[00:04:44] Ravi: competitor question — we looked at GoliathAI's multi-region offering, they offer cheaper burst pricing but their 99th percentile was worse in our tests. can Redwood match that cost?
[00:04:55] Jordan: we can get closer on unit price with longer commitments and a staged ramp; plus our caching/batching wins reduce token spend effectively lowering net cost during steady workloads.
[00:05:05] Maya: ok, let's define success criteria for the pilot: p95 < 220ms for storefront prompt templates in EU, overall cost per 1k tokens not to exceed X (we'll provide target), and KMS+audit log proof.
[00:05:17] Jordan: agree. please send the cost target and sample prompts.
[00:05:22] Maya: will do.
[00:05:24] Priya: quick ops note — Lena, we'll need the IP ranges for your VPC firewall and a contact with admin rights for the pilot.
[00:05:32] Lena: i'll get that to you today.
[00:05:34] Diego: just to capture next steps — Jordan will send updated pricing with staged commit and burst ladder, Priya will share runbook and pilot config, Orpheus provides traffic profile and targets, we'll coordinate benchmark week of 4/12.
[00:05:45] Jordan: yep i'll include optional commitment tiers (12mo, 18mo) and an escrowed burst cap that you can opt into.
[00:05:53] Ravi: how do upgrades to dedicated pools affect deployment window? if we need more GPUs mid-month, can you provision in 24–48 hours?
[00:06:00] Priya: with Dedicated we can schedule provisioning windows; urgent top-ups are possible but we try to plan a 24–72 hour window. for private it's slightly more involved due to networking.
[00:06:09] Maya: sounds fair.
[00:06:11] Jordan: anything else on the technical side?
[00:06:13] Lena: just one ask — during the pilot please don't change model variants mid-benchmark unless agreed; it skewed our last run.
[00:06:18] Priya: noted, we will freeze model variant and quantization for the benchmark unless you ask us to try an alternate.
[00:06:24] Maya: one legal/timing note — we'll need DPA and SOC2 before procurement signs. if both are in place and benchmarks pass, we can queue procurement for approval the week after results.
[00:06:36] Jordan: understood. we'll prioritize security docs.
[00:06:40] Ravi: okay, that's it from me. thanks everyone.
[00:06:43] Jordan: thanks all, we'll follow up with the artifacts and calendar invites for the benchmark.
[00:06:48] Maya: thanks, bye.
